dishes.name: Chicken bowl
dishes.rule: One base, one grain, one grilled chicken, one fresh vegetable topping and one cheese, plus whatever each chain treats as its own standard extra step — beans where the menu has a bean step, a dip where it has one. No guacamole, no chips, no extra dressing, no double protein.

dishes.name: Steak bowl
dishes.rule: The same build as the chicken bowl with the chain's standard grilled steak in place of the chicken. Nothing else changes.

dishes.name: Two slices of pepperoni
dishes.rule: Two slices of a large hand-tossed pepperoni pizza: the chain's standard large crust, its standard red pizza sauce, its regular cheese and pepperoni — nothing else, and no extra or light portions of any of them. Two slices because that is how a pizza is eaten, not how it is sold.

dishes.name: 10 boneless wings
dishes.rule: Ten boneless wings in the chain's standard hot sauce. Wingstop sauces the wing itself, so the sauce is part of the item; Buffalo Wild Wings sauces separately, so the order is ten wings plus a sauce. No fries, no dip, no celery.

dishes.name: Cheeseburger
dishes.rule: One beef patty with one slice of cheese on the chain's standard bun. Burger King, Whataburger and Sonic publish their burgers built, so the Whopper's mayo, the Whataburger's mustard and Sonic's ketchup and mayo are in these figures. Five Guys publishes parts only and treats every topping as a free extra, so it is shown bare — which is why its sodium is a third of the others'. Single patty everywhere.

dishes.name: Fried chicken sandwich
dishes.rule: Each chain's original fried chicken sandwich as it is sold — a breaded fillet on its own bun with whatever the chain puts on it as standard. Not the spicy version, not the deluxe, no cheese or bacon added.

dishes.name: Turkey sub
dishes.rule: The chain's standard turkey sandwich at its standard size — Subway's 6", Jimmy John's 8" French, Potbelly's Original — on white bread with what that chain puts on as standard. Potbelly's comes with Swiss, which is why its protein runs higher; the others are turkey only. Potbelly publishes its sandwiches with the bread removed, so the loaf is added back here.

dishes.name: Chicken salad
dishes.rule: One greens base, one grilled or roasted chicken, the chain's standard fresh tomato topping, one cheese and one vinaigrette at the pour the chain publishes. No grains, no beans, no avocado, no crunch, no double protein. Chopt and Just Salad both publish their menu salads without dressing, so every build here adds one the same way.

dishes.name: Chicken burrito
dishes.rule: The chicken bowl wrapped: the same rice, beans, grilled chicken, fresh salsa and cheese, in the chain's standard large flour tortilla instead of a bowl. Moe's publishes a separate rice portion for burritos, so that is the one used here. No guacamole, no queso, no chips.

dishes.name: Two slices of cheese
dishes.rule: Two slices of a large hand-tossed cheese pizza: the chain's standard large crust, its standard red sauce and its regular cheese, with no toppings at all. Domino's publishes a higher cheese figure for a cheese-only pizza than for one carrying toppings, and the cheese-only figure is the one used here.

dishes.name: 10 bone-in wings
dishes.rule: Ten traditional bone-in wings in the chain's standard hot sauce. Wingstop sauces the wing itself, so the sauce is part of the item; Buffalo Wild Wings sauces separately, so the order is ten wings plus a sauce. No fries, no dip, no celery. Bone-in weights include the bone, which the published figures already account for.

dishes.name: Italian sub
dishes.rule: The chain's standard Italian sandwich at its standard size — Subway's 6" Spicy Italian, Jimmy John's 8" French Vito, Potbelly's Original Italian — as it is sold, with the cured meats and cheese that come on it. These are menu items rather than builds, so each chain's own recipe stands. Potbelly publishes its sandwiches with the bread removed, so the loaf is added back here.

dishes.name: A side of fries
dishes.rule: One standard order of the chain's own plain fries — what arrives if you ask for fries and say nothing else. That is a medium at Burger King, Sonic and Chick-fil-A, the only size Whataburger publishes, and a Regular at Five Guys. The portions are not the same weight and are not meant to be: Five Guys serves 411 g where Burger King serves 200 g, and that difference is the finding rather than a flaw in the comparison. No cheese, no chili, no seasoning upgrade.

dishes.name: Chicken and rice
dishes.rule: One serving of the chain's plain rice and one grilled or roasted chicken, and nothing else — no beans, no cheese, no salsa, no sauce. The floor of a bowl order, which is what makes it comparable across chains that top their bowls very differently. Read the protein weights before the totals: a standard chicken portion is 4 oz at Chipotle but 2 oz at Cafe Rio, so Cafe Rio's lower number is half the chicken as much as it is a lighter chicken.

dishes.name: Chicken on greens
dishes.rule: One greens base and one grilled or roasted chicken, undressed — no cheese, no dressing, no crunch, no grains. Dig publishes neither a standalone cheese nor a vinaigrette, so the dressed chicken salad cannot include it; this is the build every greens chain here can make honestly, and it is also the number people are usually after.
